paper.title: Online Learning with Gaussian Payoffs and Side Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with Gaussian payoffs and side observations (general variance matrix Sigma)
unmapped: Choosing action i yields Gaussian observations X_{t,i,j} of every theta_j with known pair-dependent variance sigma_ij^2 (possibly infinite); generalizes graph feedback without self-loops
every action observable by some action with sigma_ij <= sigma
settings.definition_quote: each action $i \in \iset{K}$ is associated with some parameter $\theta_i$, and the payoff $Y_{t,i}$ to action $i$ in round $t$ is normally distributed random variable with mean $\theta_i$ and variance $\sigma^2_{ii}$, while the learner observes a $K$-dimensional Gaussian random vector $X_{t,i}$ whose $j$th coordinate is a normal random variable with mean $\theta_j$ and variance $\sigma_{ij}^2$ ... (ii) ... it knows the variance matrix $\Sigma$ in advance; (iii) $\theta \in [0,D]^K$

settings.name_in_paper: Uniform-variance partial monitoring with feedback graphs, strongly observable (lower bound)
unmapped: Self-loops not assumed (graph feedback without self-observability)
Gaussian observations with common variance sigma^2
settings.definition_quote: We will call the \emph{uniform variance} version of these problems when all the finite $\sigma_{ij}$ are equal to some $\sigma\ge 0$. ... $\Sigma$ is said to be strongly observable if $\Wea(\Sigma)=\emptyset$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 (asymptotically optimal, forced exploration with sublinear schedule beta(n))

symbols.b_theta_B: b(theta,B) = inf over c in C_{theta,B} of <c, gap(theta)>, defined via the optimisation g(theta,c)
symbols.B: uniform bound on the worst-case regret of the algorithm

source.label: thm:lb-0
source.quote: Given any $B>0$, for any algorithm such that $\sup_{\theta' \in \Theta} R_T(\theta) \le B$, we have, for any environment $\theta\in \Theta$, $R_T(\theta) \ge b(\theta,B)$.

results.notes: Implicit finite-time problem-dependent lower bound; algorithm class = algorithms with worst-case regret at most B.

symbols.bprime_theta_B: b'(theta,B) = min over c in C'_{theta,B} of <c,gap(theta)>, where C' requires sum_j c_j/sigma_ji^2 >= m_i(theta,B) for all i
symbols.B: uniform bound on the worst-case regret of the algorithm

source.label: cor:lb-0
source.quote: Given $B>0$, for any algorithm such that $\sup_{\lambda\in \Theta} R_T(\lambda) \le B$, we have, for any environment $\theta\in \Theta$, $R_T(\theta) \ge b'(\theta,B)= \min_{c\in C'_{\theta,B}}  \inprod{c}{\gap(\theta)}$.

results.notes: Relaxed interpretable version; with B = alpha T^beta it recovers the asymptotic bound up to factor (1-beta)/2.

symbols.D_max: upper end of the parameter range, theta in [0,D]^K

conditions: not the generalized full information case (some sigma_ij = infinity)

source.quote: (i) If $\Sigma$ is strongly observable, for any algorithm we have $\sup_{\theta\in \Theta}R_T(\theta) \ge \frac{\sigma\sqrt{\indp(\Sigma)T}}{8\sqrt{e}}$ for $T\ge e\sigma^2\indp(\Sigma)^3/D^2$.

results.notes: Derived from Corollary 4(i) with alpha=1/(8 sqrt e). alpha_G = independence number kappa(Sigma).

symbols.rho_dom: weak domination number rho(Sigma): size of smallest set dominating the weakly observable actions
symbols.D_max: upper end of the parameter range, theta in [0,D]^K

conditions: not the generalized full information case

source.quote: (ii) If $\Sigma$ is weakly observable,  for any algorithm we have $\sup_{\theta\in \Theta}R_T(\theta) \ge \frac{(\dom(\Sigma)D)^{1/3}(\sigma T)^{2/3} }{73\log^{2/3}K } $.

results.notes: Derived from Corollary 4(ii) with alpha=1/73; constant as printed in the paper.

symbols.c_i_eps: c_i(theta,eps) = sup of c_i(theta') over theta' within eps of theta in sup norm

source.label: thm:alg1-ub1
source.quote: For any $\theta\in \Theta$, $\epsilon>0$, $\alpha>2$ and any non-decreasing $\beta(n)$ that satisfies $0\le \beta(n)\le n/2$ and $\beta(m+n)\le \beta(m)+\beta(n)$ for $m,n\in \N$, R_T(\theta) \le ...

results.notes: Regret defined as sum E[N_i] d_i, i.e. pseudo-regret. Algorithm does not use T. Compute: solves an LP per round (assumed polynomial).

tuning: beta(n) = o(n), subadditive, and sum_s exp(-beta(s) eps^2/(2K sigma^2)) < infinity, e.g. beta(n)=a n^b

source.label: cor:alg1-asym-opt
source.quote: Suppose the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:alg1-ub1} hold. Assume, furthermore, that $\beta(n)$ satisfies $\beta(n) = o(n)$ and $\sum_{s=0}^\infty \exp \left( -\frac{\beta(s)\epsilon^2}{2K\sigma^2} \right)<\infty$ for any $\epsilon>0$, then for any $\theta$ such that $c(\theta)$ is unique, \limsup_{T\rar\infty} R_T(\theta)/\log T \le 4\alpha \inf_{c\in C(\theta)} \inprod{c}{\gap(\theta)}

results.notes: C_lin here = inf_{c in C_theta} <c, gap(theta)>, the asymptotic lower-bound constant of eq. (lb-asy).

symbols.D_max: upper end of the parameter range, theta in [0,D]^K

results.notes: R_T here denotes regret without expectation (realized pseudo-regret sum of gaps).
